scope_note: Last-resort Markley Lowell model-eligibility pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. The only retained synthesis is an exact same-account FY2026 assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even identity. It uses the directly observed four-quarter real-property bill without estimating actual public cost, cash collections, recipient distributions or net fiscal impact. Investment, construction, supplier, operations, fiscal-net, resource, community and each GDP, employment and wage candidate are rejected separately in the evidence fragment because compatible inputs, scope alignment, non-overlap proof or credible identification are unavailable.

estimates.label: FY2026 same-account assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even threshold

period.label: City of Lowell fiscal 2026 real-property assessed-liability threshold

scope.label: Real-property account P90290 for the three-building 1 Markley Way/2 Prince Avenue parcel across the same local taxing recipients

interval.interpretation: The threshold equals the directly observed four-quarter FY2026 real-property bill by definition; it is not an estimate of actual public cost, cash collected or recipient revenue.

parameters.name: same_account_property_tax_bill

provenance.detail: Sum of the four City of Lowell FY2026 real-property invoices displayed for parcel account P90290

parameters.transformation: Used unchanged as the equal-cost threshold for the same account and fiscal year

estimates.confidence_rationale: The threshold identity and complete displayed bill amount are exact, while payment-versus-adjustment status, recipient distribution and actual same-scope marginal public cost remain unknown.
estimates.decision_relevance: States the FY2026 public-cost level that would equal the parcel's assessed real-property liability without fabricating service costs or claiming a positive or negative fiscal margin.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Annual marginal fire, police, road, water, wastewater, administrative, infrastructure and financing costs assigned to the same parcel account, recipient jurisdictions and fiscal year; cash collections and recipient distributions; personal-property liability and realized exemption

derivation.formula: same-account assessed-liability public-service cost at break-even = FY2026 real-property bill = $534,231.97
assumptions: The threshold is an identity, not an observed or estimated public cost.
The hypothetical cost threshold uses the same real-property account and fiscal-year scope as the assessed liability.
Zero invoice balances are not treated as proof of payment because the portal does not distinguish payment from adjustment or abatement.

Personal-property tax, TIF savings, state credits, permit values, community gifts, utility work and indirect tax effects are not added or netted because their scope, incidence or period does not align.

limitations: This is not an estimate of actual public-service cost.
The input is a billed real-property liability, not proof of cash receipt or distribution to individual jurisdictions.
The account spans a three-building parcel and is not allocated to the selected IM3 building.
No personal-property account, annual realized abatement, marginal service demand or infrastructure cost is included.
No positive or negative net fiscal result is asserted.
estimates.notes: Conditional assessed-liability threshold only. Equality marks break-even against the FY2026 bill; actual costs and collections are unknown, so the estimate must not be summed with the underlying tax claim or presented as a fiscal surplus.
